BombVault 10.4.1 backs up a VM with Unraid snapshots in full and leaves those snapshots alone during a live backup. After a prune the local repository is readable for other users right away, and stacks are restored from the Restore page.

## ⚡ Improved

- **Stacks are restored on the Restore page.** A compose stack, whose containers come back together, has its own **Stacks** card on the Restore page, below the backups of the picked entry. The search finds a stack by its name or by any of its containers, and Backups no longer offers it. Thanks to @manilx for pointing out where people look for it. ([#399](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/bombvault/issues/399))

## 🐛 Fixed

- **A live backup keeps a VM's snapshots.** On a running VM whose disks carry Unraid snapshots, the live backup merged its temporary overlay all the way down the chain, so every snapshot ended up in the bottom image and the VM ran on that image afterwards. It merges only into the image right below, and the VM stays on its own disk with each snapshot in place. A VM without snapshots behaves as before. ([#400](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/bombvault/issues/400))
- **A VM with Unraid snapshots is backed up in full.** BombVault read only the newest file of each disk and reported success, so the backup could not be restored without the original VM. It follows each disk's backing chain, backs up every file in it and keeps Unraid's snapshot list for the VM. Restore beside the original points the restored disks at the restored files. If a chain cannot be followed to its end, the backup fails and names the file. Thanks to @schwimmbadpirat for the careful report with every check already run. ([#400](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/bombvault/issues/400))
- **The local repository stays readable after a prune.** Files that the prune after a scheduled run rewrote stayed readable by root only until the next night, so a backup tool running as another user could not copy them. BombVault makes them readable right after the prune, and also after a tag, a pull, a section move, emptying a destination and the prune that follows a delete. Flash and ZFS backups that go straight to a storage location on a mounted share get the same treatment. The config repository stays readable by root only. Thanks to @cpsmith516 for tracing the cause through the code. ([#398](https://github.com/junkerderprovinz/bombvault/issues/398))
- **Opening a repository on a host that is down gives up after 30 seconds.** A received repository or pull source on a host that did not answer held its request for up to 15 minutes while restic kept retrying. It stops after 30 seconds, like the other checks.
- **What's new lists Gotify** among the 10.4.0 changes.
